state.task: Improve weak comment information-loss and mixed-docstring judgments without changing frozen expected labels.
state.observations: Five deletion information-loss probabilities are .55-.66 despite comments carrying non-obvious rationale or caller meanings. Review context repeats each fact as observed evidence. Two private docstrings with a repeated function-name summary plus useful polarity details are kept instead of reduced. Concrete proposal preservation checks already pass five of five.

hypotheses.evidence_visibility: The model may count review-only evidence as retained documentation, so it underestimates the loss from deleting the only local rationale.
hypotheses.summary_convention: The model may keep a conventional one-line summary even though the explicitly requested source-only cleanup treats a name/signature paraphrase as redundant.

state.planned_fix: Clarify intended reader only retains actual source/doc artifacts. Reviewer context establishes truth but is not a replacement unless explicitly identified as retained accessible docs. Require clause-level treatment for private docstrings, while respecting known published/runtime consumers. Keep all current thresholds and preserve first-run results. Freeze fresh cases and blind agent baseline before testing.

best_experiment.instructions: Which experiment most directly distinguishes the reviewer-evidence visibility hypothesis from merely asking for higher scores?

criteria.counterfactual_context: Same code/comment but explicitly identify supporting context once as review-only evidence and once as retained documentation accessible to readers.
criteria.resample: Repeat calls until information-loss probabilities rise.
criteria.unknown: The proposed experiment cannot be chosen from available evidence.

separate_truth_from_availability.instructions: For measuring loss after deleting a comment, is it relevant to distinguish evidence that its statement is true from whether the intended reader can still access the statement afterwards?
